metadata.title: Draft, Not Send.
metadata.subtitle: The Handle Complaint Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to handle an incoming customer complaint, does it resolve the complaint, or hand you a draft and a suggestion? Lands the carry-out that handle-complaint is a draft-and-suggest tool, not a resolve-it tool — it drafts a response and suggests an operational fix, the same way every time, but sending the reply and making the fix stay yours.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed handling a complaint means Claude sends the reply itself. It doesn't — it drafts a response and suggests a fix. So: how do I get Claude to draft a reply to an angry customer?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is handle-complaint — a single SKILL.md file, about two kilobytes. It's the whole instruction set, written in plain language, with no hidden logic underneath it. Claude reads it, then acts on what it says. The file is the program.

Its job, word for word: pulls context on the complaint, drafts a response, and suggests an operational fix — with an optional email or ticket ID as input. Once triggered, Claude reads the Steps section and runs each one in order — linear, no branching unless a step says so.

production_viz.label: HOW IT GETS PICKED UP
production_viz.caption: reads the steps, runs them in order

beats.narration_text: Claude's job here is to draft the reply and suggest the fix — not to send anything or make the fix itself. Run the same complaint through twice, and you get the same kind of response and the same kind of fix, every time. But it only covers what the file says — anything the SKILL.md doesn't spec is outside what this skill does.

production_viz.label: DRAFTS AND SUGGESTS, NOT SENDS
production_viz.caption: it drafts the move, it doesn't make it

beats.narration_text: handle-complaint doesn't resolve a complaint — it drafts a response and suggests a fix, the same way every time; sending the reply and making the fix are still yours to do.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to handle an incoming customer complaint — read the handle-complaint skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That clause matters: having Claude explain itself first, before it acts, is how you actually see the draft and the fix it's proposing, not just the result.
